subject: german
title: Stamp 3: Data Protection and Hate Speech
welcome_lead: Stamp Germany's strict approach to data protection and online hate.
meta_desc: A-Level German adventure on DSGVO, NetzDG, and online hate speech regulation.

concepts.def: Datenschutz-Grundverordnung; EU General Data Protection Regulation effective 25 May 2018.
Data protection; a fundamental right in Germany derived from informational self-determination.
Netzwerkdurchsetzungsgesetz 2017; obliges platforms to remove illegal content quickly.
Hate speech; expressions inciting violence or hatred against groups.
Digital divide between connected and unconnected populations.
Bundesbeauftragter fur den Datenschutz und die Informationsfreiheit; federal data protection commissioner.

walkthroughs.body_html: The DSGVO took effect on 25 May 2018, harmonising EU data protection rules. It introduced rights such as access, correction, deletion, and portability, with heavy fines for violations.

The 2017 NetzDG requires large platforms to remove manifestly illegal content within 24 hours of complaint. Fines can reach 50 million EUR. Critics worry about over-blocking; supporters cite reduced hate content.
The 1983 Volkszahlungsurteil established the right to control one's personal data (Recht auf informationelle Selbstbestimmung). This shapes Germany's strict privacy culture today.
